gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's prices: Gooloo's own store sells the GOOLOO A3 for $69.99, not the $89.99 ChatGPT showed ($89.99 is the A3 Pro). Wolfbox's own store sells the MegaVolt16 Air for $179.40 and the MegaVolt 24Air (the JS24AIR card) for $278.26, not $118.69. TechGearLab measured only 51.3 Wh in the MegaVolt16 Air against a 59.2 Wh claim, so at $179.40 it costs about $3.50 per measured Wh.
standout_why: I compared against TechGearLab's MegaVolt16 Air review and its best-jump-starter list (cited), plus autoboosting, gearmyride and drivespeclab (top results). TechGearLab gives only list prices ($180 for the 16 Air, $375 for the AX65) and has no GOOLOO A3 or MegaVolt 24Air. The other three pages give no prices at all. None notes that the A3's maker price is $20 below ChatGPT's card or that the JS24AIR costs $278.26 on Wolfbox's own store. I couldn't open the cited Popular Mechanics GOOLOO page because it blocked the fetch.
decides: The GOOLOO A3 stays the value pick and is cheaper than ChatGPT said: $69.99 at gooloo.com today. The MegaVolt16 Air stays the only lab-tested pick with a compressor (TechGearLab score 77, top among compressor units), at $179.40 from the maker. The $118.69 JS24AIR card is not a maker price: the 24Air costs $278.26 at wolfbox.com, which makes it the most expensive of the three ChatGPT showed. A big-truck buyer should check the retailer's price before choosing it over the 16 Air.
candidates: Fanttik X8 APEX (Dealectric; inflator only, cannot jump-start)

HALO Bolt Air+ 1750 and Schumacher SJ1332 prices today: I didn't reach their maker pages within the tool-call budget.

Popular Mechanics' GOOLOO test results (the cited page): the fetch was blocked, so none of its measurements are used.
Fanttik X8 APEX (Dealectric's inflator) price today: I didn't open fanttik.com. It is listed as a candidate only because it inflates tires but cannot jump-start.
